items.text: Dán bealde mun luoittán sániid árppu, ja don nuppi bealde čoakkát daid.
items.q: The writer unwinds a thread of words; the reader gathers it. Does this read naturally?

items.text: Ii oktage leat heajut dilis go eadni dán máilmmis, Ipmila namas. Vare in livčče goassege ge šaddan eadnin.
items.q: Maman sighs about a mother's hard lot. Does this read naturally?

items.text: Bijan moadde sáni vel ruhtaspiinni sisa maid lean ráhkadan Niloofarii, ja rehkenastán doaivvolaččat: jus joatkkán nie, de ovdal go geassi joavdá, lea govahallama ruhtaspiidni dievva sániid.
items.q: Amir drops words into it, like coins. Is 'ruhtaspiidni' clear for a piggy bank?

items.text: Bahman lei dadjan ahte son lei humadan ovttain fakultehta professoriin, gean birra son lei gullan ahte sus lei čiekŋalis oskkáldasvuohta AmirKabir-universitehtii, ja ahte lei mearriduvvon ahte buhtadussan addojuvvošii mátkedihtor buot min guđa olbmui, geaid Konkoora sajádagat ledje olu buoret go gaskamearri, ja ahte min latnjii oastojuvvošii rátnu.
items.q: Is it clear each of the six students gets his own laptop?

items.text: Mun álo váiban gaskkas. Muhto in dadjan maidege.
items.q: A small child remembers a long walk. Does this read naturally?

items.text: Dohkket ahte don leat johkaheasta gean áddejupmi lea gussa sturrosaš.
items.q: A student insults a friend. Is 'johkaheasta' clear for a hippopotamus?

items.text: – Geahča makkár lieđđebuketta don attet čáhcái, don baikavuoiŋŋamaš.
items.q: Eskandar scolds Amir. Is it clear he means Amir made a real mess?

items.text: Olmmoš šaddá baikajorran. Mađe eanet jurddašat dan birra, dađe eanet baikajorran šaddat.
items.q: A girl jokes about a confusing painting. Is 'baikajorran' (crude for dizzy) clear?
